tour.overview:
For more than a thousand years, from 776 BC until the end of the 4th century AD, Greeks from every city gathered every four years in a wooded valley of the Peloponnese for the festival of Zeus and its athletic games. Wars were suspended by a sacred truce so athletes and spectators could travel safely. The sanctuary filled with temples, treasuries, statues of victors and training grounds, and in the Temple of Zeus stood Phidias's gold and ivory statue of the god, one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world. Olympia has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1989.

This private tour is designed for cruise passengers arriving at Katakolo, 35 kilometres away, and for travellers staying in Olympia. With a licensed archaeologist guide, you walk through the sanctuary, enter the stadium through its vaulted tunnel and stand on the original starting line, then see the museum's masterpieces, before lunch at a family winery.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 6 hours
• Start and end: the cruise port of Katakolo or your hotel in Olympia
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 4 km on flat paths

WHAT YOU SEE
• The gymnasium and the palaestra.
• The workshop of Phidias.
• The Temple of Zeus and the Temple of Hera.
• The Treasuries and the Zanes, statues paid for by cheaters' fines.
• The ancient stadium.
• The Archaeological Museum.

WHY THIS WORKS
Cruise coaches arrive at the same time; with a private car you reach the site at opening, see the stadium before the crowds and are back at the ship without stress.

WHO IT SUITS
Cruise passengers, families, sports lovers and anyone interested in ancient Greece.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you are staying longer in the Peloponnese, combine Olympia with Mycenae, Epidaurus and Nafplio on a two-day trip.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The site is shaded by pine trees but hot in summer. Running in the stadium is allowed: bring trainers if you want to race your family over the ancient 192-metre track.

days.name: The sanctuary of Zeus, the stadium of Olympia, the Archaeological Museum and a winery lunch
days.description:
What to expect: the birthplace of the Olympic Games with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and a winery lunch.

Your driver meets you on the quay at Katakolo as soon as your ship docks, or at your hotel in Olympia, and drives you 35 minutes through vineyards and olive groves to the site. Your guide meets you at the entrance. You start at the gymnasium and the palaestra, the wrestling school, where athletes trained for a month under the judges' eyes before the games. You see the workshop of Phidias, where around 430 BC the sculptor built the 12-metre statue of Zeus in gold and ivory; archaeologists found his tools and a cup inscribed 'I belong to Phidias'. A Byzantine church was later built over it.

You walk to the Temple of Zeus, whose huge column drums still lie where an earthquake threw them in the 6th century, and the older Temple of Hera, where the Olympic flame for the modern Games is lit by the rays of the sun with a parabolic mirror. You pass the row of treasuries built by Greek cities and the bases of the Zanes, bronze statues of Zeus paid for with the fines of athletes caught cheating, their names carved as a warning. Then you enter the stadium through the vaulted tunnel the athletes used. The earth banks held up to 45,000 spectators, and the stone starting and finishing lines are still in place, 192 metres apart: you can race on the original track.

In the Archaeological Museum you see the sculptures of the Temple of Zeus pediments – the chariot race of Pelops and the battle of the Lapiths and Centaurs – the Nike of Paionios and the Hermes of Praxiteles, one of the finest Greek marble statues to survive, as well as bronze helmets, including one dedicated by Miltiades, victor of Marathon. Lunch is at a family winery in the hills, with a tasting of local wines and olive oil. You are back at the ship or your hotel at about 15:00, depending on your schedule.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up at the port of Katakolo or your hotel.
09:15 – Archaeological site of Olympia (about 2 hours).
11:15 – Archaeological Museum (about 1 hour).
12:30 – Lunch and wine tasting at a family winery.
14:15 – Drive back to Katakolo.
15:00 – Back at the ship or your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• We adapt the times to your ship and plan to have you back at least one hour before all-aboard time.
• The Museum of the History of the Olympic Games can be added.
• On days with many ships, the site is busiest from 10:00; we arrive before.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, site and museum tickets, lunch with wine tasting, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: other museums, extra drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Will we be back at the ship on time?
faq.answer: Yes. Katakolo is 35 minutes from Olympia, and we plan the day to have you back at least one hour before all-aboard time. Send us your ship's times when you book.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the archaeological site and the Archaeological Museum.

faq.question: Can we run in the stadium?
faq.answer: Yes. Running on the ancient track is allowed and great fun; bring suitable shoes.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch with a wine tasting at a family winery. Non-alcoholic drinks and vegetarian or other diets are available.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 4 km on flat, partly shaded paths.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love racing in the stadium and the stories of cheating athletes. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The site is flat with gravel paths, and the museum is accessible. The tunnel to the stadium has a slight slope.

faq.question: Can we see where the Olympic flame is lit?
faq.answer: Yes, the altar in front of the Temple of Hera, where the flame for each modern Games is lit by the sun a few months before the opening.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes, a hat and sun cream in summer.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. Spring is green and full of flowers; summer is hot, so we arrive early.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour, and at no cost if your ship cannot call at Katakolo. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
